context: Algebraic construction of Z as the additive group completion of N
editorial_note: ProofWiki formally constructs integers as the inverse completion of natural numbers. This equivalence relation is independent of rational numbers and gives explicit representatives without assuming integer subtraction already exists. The induced addition and multiplication require separate well-definedness checks, so this is an independently described construction, not a proof the resulting quotient is an integral domain.
text: Define an equivalence relation on N×N by (a,b)∼(c,d) precisely when a+d=b+c. The integers can be constructed as equivalence classes Z=(N×N)/∼, with [a,b] representing the formal difference a−b.

context: Commutative unital integral domain Z under integer addition and multiplication
editorial_note: The dedicated ProofWiki ring-of-integers definition introduces the integer ring and directs readers to theorems that verify its ring and integral-domain properties. The structural assertion that (Z,+,·) is an integral domain is a theorem/property, not itself the definition of integer ring; it must remain distinguishable in publication from the bare named structure.
text: The ring of integers is the algebraic structure (Z,+,·), where Z is the set of integers, + is integer addition, and · is integer multiplication. It is a commutative ring with identity 1 and no zero divisors.

context: Equivalence-class fractions and universal property of an integral-domain fraction field
editorial_note: Stacks Project Example 9.3.4 gives explicit fraction equivalence and the universal property; ProofWiki gives an independently checked field-of-quotients formulation involving an injective embedding into a field. The construction requires D to be an integral domain to support the equivalence criterion and well-defined inverses of nonzero classes. Q is the instance D=Z; general fraction fields and total quotient rings for rings with zero divisors are not the same context.
text: For a commutative integral domain D, its fraction field Frac(D) can be constructed from pairs (a,b) with a∈D and b∈D\{0}, identifying (a,b) with (c,d) when ad=bc. The class of (a,b) is denoted a/b. Addition and multiplication of these classes yield a field into which D embeds as a subring.

context: Fraction field of integral domain: equivalent universal mapping property
editorial_note: ProofWiki Definition:Field of Quotients, Definition 3, gives the universal property with the embedding as part of the data. The quantifier requires an injective D→K map so all nonzero denominator images are invertible. The morphism is required to be a field homomorphism compatible with the embeddings; this is equivalent to the fraction-pair construction after existence is shown, but is not a definition of the total quotient ring of an arbitrary ring with zero divisors.
text: For an integral domain D, a fraction field may equivalently be specified as a field F with an injective ring homomorphism i:D→F such that, for every field K and injective ring homomorphism j:D→K, there is a unique field homomorphism h:F→K satisfying h∘i=j. This universal mapping property characterizes the fraction field together with its embedding of D.
